paths.pg: The pool is the Db's alone: obtain a handle with db.handle(schema) instead. Fastify and Drizzle are public API; pg is not.
paths.jose: Building a JWS is Signatures' alone: ask it for one with signatures.sign(typ, claims). Decisions stores the string it answers with and never touches the format, and a second party assembling segments is a second chance to emit something nobody else can verify.

patterns.message: Nostr belongs to the two parts that speak it, the Nostr Channel and Nostr Auth, the way pg belongs to the Db: nothing from either library crosses this framework's API boundary, so they are ordinary dependencies rather than peers, and a third part reaching for one would make them something a consumer has to install. src/test-support/** is exempt too, because a real client is the only thing that proves the fake Relay is a Relay and a real signer the only thing that proves a NIP-98 forgery is refused.
